title: Bring every rule to one form

blocks.text: A depot's ordering tool collects rules from several planners. Some write "at most", some "at least", some "exactly". The checker from the previous practice only understands one form, rows of $`Ax \le b`$, so every rule has to be brought to it first.
Write `to_leq(rules, n)` in `leq.py`. Each rule is a triple `(coeffs, sense, limit)`:

items: `coeffs` maps a variable's index (0 to `n - 1`) to its coefficient; a variable not in `coeffs` has coefficient 0;

blocks.text: Return `(A, b)` as NumPy arrays, `A` with shape `(rows, n)`, where each row means $`a^\top x \le b`$:

headers: rows it becomes, in this order

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from leq import to_leq

# A kitchen orders three ingredients; x[j] is how many crates of ingredient j.
rules = [
    ({0: 3, 1: 2, 2: 1}, "<=", 30),   # fridge space
    ({0: 1, 2: 1}, ">=", 4),          # at least 4 crates of ingredients 0 and 2
    ({1: 1}, "==", 2),                # exactly 2 crates of ingredient 1
]
A, b = to_leq(rules, 3)
print("A rows:", A.tolist())
print("b:", b.tolist())

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np

Rule = tuple[dict[int, float], str, float]


def to_leq(rules: list[Rule], n: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Write rules over n variables as one A and one b with every row in the form a @ x <= b."""
    # TODO: one or two rows per rule, depending on its sense (see the statement).
    return np.zeros((0, n)), np.zeros(0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    A, b = to_leq([({0: 1, 1: 1}, "<=", 4), ({0: 1}, ">=", 1)], 2)
    print(A)
    print(b)

cases.says: rules that are already at most a limit become rows unchanged
an at-least rule becomes one row with its coefficients and its limit negated
an exactly rule becomes two rows, the at-most row first
every one of the n variables has a column, even one no rule mentions

origin.section: Every Linear Rule Fits Ax ≤ b: Flip ≥ Rows, Split = Rows

concepts: at-least rules are negated on both sides and exactly rules become an at-most row and a negated row
